EMERGENCY CRITERIA
A LEVEL (1) EMERGENCY  AT THE SILVERBERRY SITE IS A STATE THAT WOULD
FORCE NORMAL OPERATIONS TO BE TEMPORARILY SUSPENDED
OR SHUT DOWN.
A LEVEL (1) EMERGENCY WOULD PRESENT NO DANGER TO C.C.S.
PERSONNEL OR TO THE PUBLIC AROUND OR NEAR THE SILVERBERRY
SITE.
C.C.S. PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT WOULD CONTROL A LEVEL (1)
EMERGENCY ON SITE.
A LEVEL 2 EMERGENCY  IS ANY STATE, WHICH HAS THE POTENTIAL TO EXTEND
BEYOND THE BOUNDARIES OF C.C.S. PROPERTY AT
SILVERBERRY.
A LEVEL 2 EMERGENCY AT SILVERBERRY WOULD PRESENT NO
IMMEDIATE DANGER TO THE PUBLIC.
A LEVEL 2 EMERGENCY WOULD REQUIRE EXTERNAL SUPPORT SERVICE
SUCH AS FIRE OR AMBULANCE TO ATTEND TO THE SILVERBERRY SITE.
A LEVEL 3 EMERGENCY  STATE IS SUCH THAT CONTROL IS LOST ON THE SITE
AND THE EMERGENCY HAS EXTENDED THE BOUNDARIES OF THE
SILVERBERRY SITE.
EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN CONTENTS
THE SILVERBERRY EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN WILL INCLUDE THE
FOLLOWING:

CCS will designate an environmental inspector to ensure that this C&R plan and any
other applicable environmental requirements are adhered to.

1) To mitigate the potential impacts, topsoil will be salvaged from all areas that will
be disturbed by landfill construction.

3) All salvaged topsoil will be stored in discreet piles during construction and will be
protected from erosion by seeding with a temporary cover mix, or by use of a
tackifier.   All salvaged topsoil piles will be clearly marked with staking and will be
kept separate from subsoil or grade piles.  Should a reduction in soil binding lead
to wind erosion of topsoil, tackifier may be re-applied or other contingency
measures implemented as appropriate to avoid soil loss.

4)   All soils to be retained for fi nal reclamation will be r etained in lo w (<2m) berms
and will be seeded to protect against erosion and promote long-term healthy soil
conditions.
1) All construction activities will be restricted to the designated surveyed project site.
All construction traffic will adhere to safety and traffic regulations.

2) To prevent introduction of weedy species to the area, all equipment will be
washed with high pressure water or steam to remove any remnant mud and
vegetative debris prior to entering the project site.  Equipment will not be allowed
on the project site if has not been properly cleaned.

4) Adequate fire fighting equipment will be available on site.  In the event of a fire,
the Contractor will immediately use resources required to contain the fire.  The
Emergency Response Plan will be activated if any fire cannot be immediately
controlled.

5) If a previously unidentified archaeological and/or heritage site is encountered
during construction, no further construction will be undertaken in the immediate
vicinity until the site has been examined by a qualified archaeologist.
Construction activity will not re-commence without consultation with the BC
Archaeological Planning and Assessment Branch.

6) Prior to the start of construction activity, site boundaries will be clearly staked to
prevent disturbance to unauthorized areas.

7) If conditions become such that significant erosion is occurring during construction,
erosion control measures such as silt fences, straw bales, or other suitable means
will be used to control the erosion.

1) The servicing and fueling of equipment or storage of fuel will be not be allowed
within 50 metres of the on-site runoff pond.

3) Prior to commencement of the activity, all equipment (e.g., generators, pumps) or
servicing activities with the potential for accidental spills (e.g., oil changes,
hydraulic repair, coolants, etc.) must have appropriate containment methods in
place (i.e., storage containers, impervious tarps, berms, etc.).

4) Used oil, filter and grease cartridges, lubrication containers, and other products of
equipment maintenance and/or repair will be collected and disposed of at an
appropriate facility.

5) All hazardous material stored on the project site will be labelled according to TDG
(Transportation of Dangerous Goods) and WHMIS (Workplace Hazardous
Materials Information System) regulations.

6) To ensure adequate response capability in the event of a fuel spill, all fuel
transport vehicles and Contractor foreman vehicles will carry a minimum of 10
kilograms of suitable commercial sorbent material.

7) All spills of fuel, oil, hazardous chemicals or materials will be reported immediately
to an on-site supervisor who will then report the incident, as necessary, to CCS
Silverberry, BC Ministry of Water, Land and Air Protection and local municipal
authorities.

8) In the event of a spill, the contractor will be required to make all resources
available to contain and clean up the spill.  Traffic will be minimized in and around
the spill site.

9) All ground spills will be contained as quickly as possible through dyking, suction
methods (vacuum trucks), excavation and the use of absorbents or other
appropriate recovery techniques.

10) Any contaminated vegetation, soil, and used sorbent materials will be collected
and disposed of at an approved facility, or will be stored within the approved
facility pending final disposal after landfill completion.

1) CCS Silverberry will keep all appropriate regulatory personnel and adjacent
landowners informed of project developments throughout all phases of
construction.

1) Project related wildlife deaths and nuisance animals will be reported immediately
to the appropriate British Columbia Ministry of Water, Land and Air Protection,
Wildlife Branch representative.

2) The feeding or harassment of livestock or wildlife will be prohibited.  Construction
personnel will not be permitted to have firearms or pets on the project site.  All
food and wastes will be stored and secured in vehicles or appropriate facilities.

1) All garbage and construction debris will be collected and disposed of in
accordance with manufacturer specifications and regulatory requirements.

3) Removed surface material will be evenly redistributed over the disturbed area,
except where it is being retained in low berms for final post-decommissioning site
reclamation.

1) CCS Silverberry will use Certified Canada No. 1 seed in its seed mixes.
Certificates of seed analysis will be requested for all seed mixes and allotments
purchased by CCS.  This limits the introduction of prohibited or noxious weeds.
The actual seed mixes used will be developed following discussions with British
Columbia Ministry of Water, Land and Air Protection representatives, and
considering seed species availability.

2) CCS will evaluate the success of re-vegetation and efforts after one full growing
season and conduct any remedial work as required.

3) As necessary, weed control measures will be undertaken within the area of
disturbance.

5.3.2 Operations Manual
The following is an example of the contents of a typical Operations Manual for a CCS
facility.  A similar plan will be developed for the CCS Silverberry facility, including both
the landfarm and landfill .

1. Compliance Verification and Reporting
1.1 The Holder must provide to the EAO any document, data or information requested by
the EAO for the purposes of compliance inspection and verification. The Holder must
provide any document, data or information requested within the timeframe and in the
manner specified by the EAO.
1.2 The Holder must submit a report to the attention of the EAO on the status of
compliance with this Amendment at the following times:
a) At least 30 days prior to the start of Construction; and,
b) On or before January 31 in each year after the start of Construction, until three
years after the start of Operations.
1.3 The reports in subsection 1.2 must be in a form satisfactory to the EAO. The EAO may
adjust or extend this reporting requirement by providing written notice to the Holder.

2. Expansion Status Notification
2.1 The Holder must notify the EAO in writing that the Expansion is in Construction and
Operations. The notification must be received by the EAO within 30 days of the
commencement of Construction and Operations.
2.2 Should the primary contact for the Expansion change, the Holder must notify the EAO,
in writing, within 30 days of such change and provide the physical address, e-mail
address and phone number(s) of the new primary contact.

3. Compliance Notification
3.1 The Holder must notify the EAO as soon as practical and, in any event no more than
72 hours, after the Holder determines that the Holder has not, or may not have, fully
complied with this Amendment.

4. Document Review and Implementation
4.1 Where a condition of this Amendment requires the Holder to provide a Document, the
Holder must provide the Document to the EAO in the timeframe referenced in such
condition, unless otherwise approved by the EAO.
4.2 The EAO may, within 45 days of receiving a copy of such Document referred to
subsection 4.1, advise that:
a) the Holder may proceed to implement the Document with or without revisions; or
b) a revised Document must be provided for approval of the EAO prior to a specified
activity or milestone.
4.3 If the EAO advises pursuant to subsection 4.2 that changes are required to a
Document, then the Holder must follow the instructions of the EAO in that regard.
4.4 If the EAO does not advise on subsection 4.2 within 45 days of the EAO receiving a
Document, the Holder may proceed to implement the Document unless approval of the
Document is required by the condition before the Document is implemented.
4.5 The Holder may, or the EAO may require the Holder to, revise any Document if the
Holder or the EAO determines that the implementation of the Document is not:
a) meeting one or more objectives of the Document set out in the relevant condition of
this Amendment or in the Document as required by subsection 5.1(a);
b) having the effects contemplated or intended, as set out in the Document itself;
c) consistent with the Amendment; or
d) consistent with changes in industry best practices or technology.

5. Plan Development
5.1 Where a condition of this Amendment requires the Holder to develop a Document, any
such Document must, at a minimum, include the following information:
a) purpose and objectives of the Document;
b) roles and responsibilities of the Holder, project personnel and contractors;
c) names and, if applicable, professional certifications and professional stamps/seals,
of those responsible for the preparation of the Document;
d) schedule for implementing the Document throughout the relevant project phases;
e) how the effectiveness of the mitigation measures will be evaluated including the
schedule for evaluating effectiveness;
f) an adaptive management plan to address effects of the Expansion if the monitoring
conducted under subsection 5.2 of this condition shows that those effects:
i. are not mitigated to the extent contemplated in the Amendment Application; or
ii. are not predicted in the Amendment Application;
g) schedules and methods for the submission of reporting to specific agencies,
Indigenous Nations and the public and the required form and content of those
reports; and,
h) process and timing for updating and revising the Document, including any
consultation with agencies and Indigenous Nations that would occur in connection
with such updates and revisions.
5.2 Where a Document includes monitoring requirements, the Document must include:
a) description of baseline information that will be used to support monitoring of the
effectiveness of mitigation;
b) methodology, location, frequency, timing and duration of monitoring; and,
c) scope, content and frequency of reporting of the monitoring results.

6. Consultation
6.1 Where a condition of this Amendment requires the Holder to consult a particular party
or parties regarding the content of a Document, the Holder must, to the satisfaction of
the EAO:
a) provide written notice to each such party that:
i. includes a copy of the Document;
ii. invites the party to provide its views on the content of such Document; and
iii. indicates:
A) if a timeframe providing such views to the Holder is specified in the relevant
condition of this Amendment, that the party may provide such views to the
Holder within such time frame; or
B) if a timeframe providing such views to the Holder is not specified in the
relevant condition of this Amendment, specifies a reasonable period during
which the party may submit such views to the Holder;
b) undertake a full and impartial consideration of any views and other information
provided by a party in accordance with the timelines specified in a notice given
pursuant to subsection 6.1(a);
c) provide a written explanation to each such party that provided comments in
accordance with a notice given pursuant to subsection 6.1(a) as to:
i. how the views and information provided by such party to the Holder have been
considered and addressed in a revised version of the Document; or
ii. why such views and information have not been addressed in a revised version of
the Document;
d) maintain a record of consultation with each such party regarding the Document; and
e) provide a copy of such consultation record to the EAO, the relevant party, or both,
promptly upon the written request of the EAO or such party. The copy of such
consultation record must be provided to the EAO, relevant party, or both, no later
than 15 days after the Holder receives the request for a copy of the consultation
record, unless otherwise authorized by the EAO.

9. Contaminants Management Plan
9.1 The Holder must retain a Qualified Professional to develop a plan for contaminants
management and monitoring. The plan must be developed in consultation with ENV,
NH, and Indigenous Nations.
9.2 The plan must include at least the following:
a) the name, organization, and qualifications of the proposed Qualified Professional
responsible for the development and implementation of this plan;
b) methods, including type, timing, frequency and spatial boundaries, both inside and
outside the Expansion footprint, of pre-construction surveys. These pre-construction
surveys must include:
i. vegetation surveys for identification of pollutant concentrations and distribution of
potential impacts to vegetation;
ii. air quality surveys for identification of pollutant concentration and distribution of
potential impacts to ambient air quality, including volatile organic compounds and
criteria air contaminants;
iii. soil surveys for identification of pollutant concentrations, including barium, and
distribution of potential impacts to surficial soils;
iv. surface water surveys for identification of pollutant concentration and distribution
of potential impacts to surface water; and
v. ground water quality baseline surveys for identification of pollutant concentration
and distribution of potential impacts to ground water;
c) results of the pre-construction surveys described in subsection 9.2(b), including
identification of contaminants of potential concern (COPCs) for ongoing monitoring;
d) the timing, method and process to developing early detection COPC benchmarks to
determine if any exceedances of the benchmarks observed during monitoring are
related to the Expansion, using the results of the pre-construction surveys;
e) a requirement that exceedances in subsection 9.2(d) related to the Expansion will
trigger an assessment of potential human health risks and a hydrogeology impact
assessment and must include additional monitoring and mitigation measurers aimed
at addressing the exceedances as a form of adaptive management required by
section 5.1(f). The plan must include the timing, method and process for the
assessment of potential human health risks and hydrogeology impact assessment;
f) the means by which the mitigation measures listed in the Amendment Application in
Sections 4.6 (Terrestrial vegetation), 4.2 (Air Quality), 4.1 (Terrain and Soils), 4.4
(Surface Water); and 4.5 (Groundwater)

10. Country Foods Monitoring Plan
10.1 The Holder must retain a Qualified Professional to develop a plan for country foods
monitoring. The plan must be developed in consultation with NH and Indigenous
Nations.
10.2 The plan must include at least the following:
a) the name, organization, and qualifications of the proposed Qualified Professional
responsible for the development and implementation of this plan;
b) methods, including type, timing, frequency and spatial boundaries, both inside and
outside the Expansion footprint, of pre-construction surveys for country foods.
These pre-construction surveys must include:
i. identification of country foods to be sampled;
ii. identification of COPCs in country foods identified in 10.2(b)(i);
iii. identification of appropriate COPC monitoring levels for human health (risk and
exposure);
iv. how any surveys and results required by Condition 9 were used to inform the
requirements of this plan;
c) results of the pre-construction surveys described in subsection 10.2(b);
d) the means by which the mitigation measures in the Amendment Application (Section
8.5.1 Human Health) will be implemented;
e) the identification of additional mitigation measures needed to reduce exceedances
of COPC monitoring levels for human health (risk and exposure) caused by the
Expansion relative to pre-construction surveys in subsection 10.2(b)(i) to below
levels identified in 10.2(b)(iii); and,
f) monitoring during Construction and Operations for exceedances of COPC levels for
human health (risk and exposure) relative to the pre-construction surveys described
in subsection 10.2(b).
10.3  The Holder must provide this draft plan to the EAO, NH, and Indigenous Nations for
review a minimum of 90 days prior to the planned commencement of Construction.
10.4 The plan, and any amendments thereto, must be implemented to the satisfaction of a
Qualified Professional and to the satisfaction of the EAO throughout Construction and
Operations.
